- **198.51.100.30 (card-testing, quieter):** 1,350 `POST /checkout/payment` behind a spoofed Chrome UA — same abuse, lower rate to stay under thresholds.

**WAF log review — `d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net` (WebACL `CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4`), 2026-10-10 17:00–18:15 UTC**

**What looks malicious** — all 169,927 requests came from just **4 US IPs, every one hostile**, matching the hunt's three themes:
- **Card-testing:** `198.51.100.10` (Artillery, 168,126 reqs ≈ 99% of traffic, flooding the checkout funnel incl. 9,262 `POST /checkout/payment`) and `198.51.100.30` (1,350 `POST /checkout/payment`, Chrome-spoofed).
- **Scan:** `198.51.100.20` enumerating secrets/configs (`/.env`, `/.aws/credentials`, `/.git/config`, `/actuator/heapdump`, `/backup.sql`, …).
- **Injection:** `198.51.100.60` (sqlmap) with `UNION SELECT` SQLi and `<script>` XSS.

**What it detected but did NOT block:**
- The rate rule **`AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront` is in COUNT mode** — it matched the entire 168,126-request flood (~37× its 300/5-min limit) and allowed every request.
- The AntiDDoS set labeled 126,090 requests `challengeable-request` but took no action.
- Gaps that slipped through *undetected*: `198.51.100.30`'s 1,350 payment POSTs (under the limit, not even counted) and ~200 of the scanner's probes.

**Mitigation (validated, ready to apply):** The specialist's primary fix is to **flip the rate-based rule from Count to Block** on WebACL `CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4`, leaving all managed rule groups untouched — this converts the existing detection into active throttling and would have stopped the flood. # Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Single IP flooded the distribution (~168K requests)
**Description:** A single source, 198.51.100.10 (US), sent ~168,126 requests (~98.9% of all traffic) in a flat ~11,000/5-min profile (~2,240 req/min) across the whole 17:00–18:15 UTC window. User-agent attribution identifies it as the **Artillery load-testing tool** ("Artillery (https://artillery.io)"). The traffic is a realistic e-commerce browse/checkout mix and is benign stress-test traffic — but it was entirely unmitigated (all ALLOWED) because the rate rule is Count-only.
**Time:** 2026-10-10T17:00:00Z - 2026-10-10T18:15:00Z

### Sensitive-file path scanning from 198.51.100.20
**Description:** ~225 probes for secret/config files — /.env, /.aws/credentials, /id_rsa, /.git/config, /wp-config.php.bak, /actuator/heapdump and similar. Only ~25 were blocked; many sensitive paths were ALLOWED, indicating a WAF coverage gap for secret-file scanning.
**Time:** 2026-10-10T17:00:00Z

### Card-testing / checkout abuse on POST /checkout/payment
**Description:** Two actors abused the checkout funnel. **198.51.100.10** (UA `Artillery (artillery.io)`) drove the dominant checkout-abuse/card-testing flood — walking the full funnel (GET /catalog → POST /cart → POST /checkout → POST /checkout/delivery → 9,262× POST /checkout/payment) at ~37 req/s, all ALLOWED. **198.51.100.30** (spoofed Chrome UA) is a quieter card-tester: 1,350× POST /checkout/payment that matched NO WAF rule and stayed under the rate limit, so WAF had zero visibility into it.
**Time:** 2026-10-10T17:00:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: Count-only rate-based rule allowed a single-IP flood through
**Description:** The rate-based rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront is in COUNT mode (limit 300/5-min per IP). The flood source 198.51.100.10 is the Artillery load-testing tool (UA "Artillery (https://artillery.io)"), which sustained ~2,240 req/min for the full window and passed entirely. In Count mode the rule detected but did not block any of it.
**Cascades to:** symptom-ip-flood, symptom-cardtest

#### Supporting Observations
- **Rate-based rule counted 168,584 requests but blocked none (Count mode):** The rate-based rule **AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront** (limit 300 per 5-min per IP) matched **168,584** requests in **COUNT** mode during the window. Because the rule action is Count rather than Block, it recorded the breach but applied no throttling \u2014 the flooding IP was never rate-limited.

### Cause: Managed rules let many sensitive-file probes through
**Description:** AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet / KnownBadInputsRuleSet blocked only ~25 of ~225 secret-file probes from 198.51.100.20. Sensitive paths such as /.aws/credentials, /id_rsa, /actuator/env, and /.git/config were ALLOWED — a managed-rule coverage gap for secret/config-file scanning.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Switch the rate-based rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront (Priority 1) in WebACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 from Action=Count to Action=Block, so source IPs exceeding 300 requests per 5-minute window are throttled instead of only counted. All existing managed rule groups are preserved unchanged.

## Reasoning
The rate-based rule is in Count mode and detected but did not block the 198.51.100.10 (Artillery) flood of 168,126 requests (~99% of traffic, ~37x the 300/5-min limit), including a sustained checkout-funnel card-testing pattern (9,262 POST /checkout/payment, 9,257 POST /checkout, 9,260 POST /checkout/delivery, 14,678 POST /cart). Flipping it to Block converts existing detection into active throttling. Managed rule groups (AntiDDoS, AmazonIpReputationList, CommonRuleSet, KnownBadInputs, SQLiRuleSet) are already in block/override-none mode and left untouched.
